evidence: Quote is real but sits in Sec. IV 'Evaluating Agent-Generated Repairs' (run-in 'Patch Correctness'), not Sec. III-C (III-C = 'Evaluation Framework for Historic Bugs'). Plausible = passes bug-reproducing tests; valid = semantically equivalent to ground truth. Table IV reports both rates.
correction: Location: Sec. IV (definitions + 'three of the authors'), Sec. V-A and Table IV (plausible vs valid rates). Authors Rondon, Wei, Cambronero, Cito, Sun, Sanyam, Tufano, Chandra; arXiv 2501.07531 (2025); venue ICSE-SEIP 2025 [verify].

evidence: Abstract: 'TestGen-LLM verifies that its generated test classes successfully clear a set of filters...'; '73% of its recommendations being accepted for production deployment by Meta software engineers.'
correction: Phrase as '73% of TestGen-LLM recommendations (all of which had passed its filters) accepted for production'. Published FSE 2024 Companion (Industry) [verify].

evidence: Blog (Jia, Mao, Harman, 13 Sep 2018): 'When its patches are fully tested, SapFix sends them to a human reviewer for approval'; 'it is not designed to deploy fixes to production code on its own.'
correction: Key implies Marginean et al. ICSE-SEIP 2019 paper, but the URL is the 2018 Meta Engineering blog by Yue Jia, Ke Mao, Mark Harman; cite as such or cite the ICSE-SEIP paper separately.

evidence: Sec. V-C: 'Initially, integrators treat the existence of testing code in the pull request as a positive signal. Success of test runs by a continuous integration system also reinforces trust'. Sec. VI-B: prior work found test inclusion 'was not a strong factor'.
correction: Gousios, Zaidman, Storey, van Deursen, ICSE 2015. Location: Sec. V-C (RQ3) and Sec. VI-B 'Testing'.

evidence: Numbers verified in PDF Sec. 3.1 (Results): 'The most important factor influencing the pull request decision is same_user (with 31% variance).' and 'ci_failed_perc stands out, explaining 18% of the variance' (column 6, Table 5).
correction: Location is Sec. 3.1 (Results), Table 5 — not Sec. 4 (Sec. 4 is Discussion). Authors Zhang, Yu, Gousios, Rastogi; arXiv 2105.13970; later IEEE TSE [verify]. Note 31% is share of explained variance in the basic model.

evidence: Table 2 (developers, importance): steps to reproduce (83%), stack traces (57%), test cases (51%). Sec. 3.2 (reporters): 'capture/replay tools which record test cases [16, 25, 38] should be integrated into bug tracking systems.'
correction: Developers rated steps to reproduce (83%) most important, then stack traces (57%) and test cases (51%); from reporter data (Sec. 3.2) the authors suggest integrating capture/replay tools that record test cases into bug trackers.

evidence: Blog (14 Jul 2025): AI slop 'about 20% of all submissions'; 'In early July, about 5% of the submissions in 2025 had turned out to be genuine vulnerabilities.'
correction: Specify: curl HackerOne security submissions, 2025 through early July.

evidence: TL;DR: 'Current QEMU project policy is to DECLINE any contributions which are believed to include or derive from AI generated content'; body: 'will decline any contribution if use of AI is either known or suspected.'
correction: Policy excludes AI use for research/analysis/debugging whose output is not included in contributions; cite as living doc (docs/master), accessed 2026-10-21.
